# Scientific evidence rubric

This prospective rubric applies only to new experiments. It does not regrade old
cohorts. Each applicable cell has three independently reviewed binary criteria
in matrix_rubric.py; report a vector of 0–3 values, never an eight-cell total.
An unreviewed cell is null, not zero. A missing claim receives zero only after an
explicit reviewer determination. Equivalent mathematics and terminology count;
matching the author's equations or mechanism names is not required.

The review archive must contain the frozen submission, executable hash check,
observations, prospective journal and independent predictions. A hash supplied
by the candidate alone is not verification. Each positive criterion requires a
claim reference, a concrete evidence locator and a scientific rationale. The
aggregator checks record integrity only: it cannot judge whether evidence is
correct or sufficient. Fresh result-to-claim review remains same-family and
provisional. The three checks per cell are an initial rubric, not a validated
psychometric scale; report reviewer uncertainty and disagreement separately.

| Cell | Requirements, one point each |
|---|---|
| Law / deduction | Scoped quantitative relationship; derivation with units and assumptions; independent numerical prediction supports it. |
| Law / mechanism | Coupled state equations; consistent conserved flux accounting; a legal control distinguishes a stated rival. |
| Law / unification | One frozen parameterization; predictions across at least two distinct controlled regimes; rival and failure scope analyzed. |
| Law / counterfactual | Legal intervention and comparator specified; effect predicted before observation; matched control supports sign and magnitude within stated uncertainty. |
| Structure / deduction | Operational dependence graph; explicit observable consequence derived; a competing graph compared using evidence. |
| Structure / mechanism | Scoped pathway claim; mediator or context control separates a stated explanation; observational equivalence limits stated. |
| Structure / unification | Shared graph across at least two regimes; changes in context-dependent influence accounted for; competing graph and scope assessed. |
| Structure / counterfactual | Legal node/context manipulation; structural consequence predicted prospectively; matched experiment supports it. |

“Structure” refers to effective dependence and carbon-flow pathways among
observable species/metabolites, not molecular pathways. Species removal and
initial-condition/feed changes are legal; arbitrary internal edge deletion is
not. A three-way context interaction alone does not prove a unique microscopic
three-body process. Unobserved mediators and state-dependent effective pairwise
representations can be observationally equivalent. Such alternatives must not
be scored wrong merely for differing from the simulator implementation.

A mechanistic criterion cannot be earned solely by accurate prediction or a
named graph. Conservation can be checked analytically; causality requires legal
controlled evidence, including confounding and noise discussion. Sparse tests
do not establish a uniform law over all legal conditions. An inconclusive
scientific conclusion is allowed and may support an honestly scoped claim,
but it does not automatically satisfy a discrimination criterion.

Prediction RMSE, service failures, invalid programs and acquisition costs are
reported separately. No new model run has yet been graded with this rubric.
